## docs/issue-4-architecture-baseline...origin/docs/issue-4-architecture-baseline
ae75c13 (HEAD -> docs/issue-4-architecture-baseline, origin/docs/issue-4-architecture-baseline) docs(architecture): define MVP system baseline
 docs/PRD.md          |   2 +-
 docs/architecture.md | 467 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 468 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
   115	- SQLite adapter: persist and retrieve the approved record projection.
   116	- OpenAI adapter: generate and validate a sanitized structured explanation.
   117	
   118	External client objects remain behind these adapters so unit tests can use
   119	deterministic fakes.
   120	
   121	## 4. Scan state flow
   122	
   123	One application instance runs at most one active scan. A second start request
   124	receives a structured conflict response. This bounds resource use and keeps
   125	Core behavior explicit.
   126	
   127	```mermaid
   128	stateDiagram-v2
   129	    [*] --> QUEUED: Persist scan
   130	    QUEUED --> RUNNING: Start asynchronous work
   131	    state RUNNING {
   132	        [*] --> LOADING_DESIRED
   133	        LOADING_DESIRED --> READING_LIVE
   134	        READING_LIVE --> COMPARING
   135	        COMPARING --> SAVING_RESULT
   136	    }
   137	    RUNNING --> COMPLETED
   138	    RUNNING --> FAILED
   139	```
   140	
   141	Explanation state is subordinate to, and independent of, scan execution:
   142	
   143	```mermaid
   144	stateDiagram-v2
   145	    [*] --> NOT_REQUESTED
   146	    NOT_REQUESTED --> REQUESTED: Manual operator action
   147	    REQUESTED --> SAVED
   148	    REQUESTED --> EXPLANATION_FAILED
   149	```
   150	
   151	The public execution statuses remain `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `COMPLETED`, and
   152	`FAILED`. Named running stages provide progress without creating additional
   153	execution statuses.
   154	
   155	The start request persists `QUEUED` before returning `202 Accepted`. A
   156	self-hosted Next.js Route Handler schedules
   157	`after(() => scanService.run(scanId))`; the long-lived Node.js process
   158	continues the scan while the UI polls. Graceful shutdown allows a bounded
   159	10–30 second drain, but Core does not resume unfinished work after termination.
   160	
   161	Core has no overall workflow timeout, automatic retry, cancellation, or
   162	restart resumability. Each GitHub, Kubernetes, and OpenAI transport call still
   163	uses a bounded client or abort timeout so one hung dependency cannot occupy
   164	the sole active-scan slot indefinitely.
   165	
   166	An explanation is a separate manual operation available only for
   167	`IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE`. Explanation failure is persisted
   168	without changing the completed scan or deterministic outcome.
   169	
   170	## 5. Desired and live state
   171	
   172	### GitHub desired state
   173	
   174	Core uses native server-side `fetch` against the GitHub REST API:
   175	
   176	1. accept a branch or commit SHA for the deployment-configured repository;
   177	2. resolve it to an immutable commit SHA;
   178	3. retrieve exactly one configured relative manifest path at that SHA; and
   179	4. parse exactly one YAML document.
   180	
   181	The adapter allowlists GitHub, the configured repository identity, and a safe
   182	relative path. It does not clone repositories, invoke shell Git, follow
   183	arbitrary hosts, or accept embedded credentials. Public reads work without
   184	authentication; an optional server-side token may be configured without
   185	entering persisted product data or browser responses.
   186	
   187	### Kubernetes live state
   188	
   189	Core uses `@kubernetes/client-node` and a server-configured kubeconfig path to
   190	read the Deployment derived from the desired manifest:
   191	
   192	- API group and version: `apps/v1`;
   193	- kind: `Deployment`;
   194	- identity: explicit desired namespace and name; and
   195	- operation: one read of the matching Deployment.
   196	
   197	The demo credential is read-only and namespace-scoped. Kubernetes
   198	authorization—not application intent alone—must prevent mutation. Missing
   199	Deployment is translated to `MISSING_LIVE`; authentication, authorization, and
   200	availability failures remain execution failures.
   201	
   202	## 6. Persistence boundary
   203	
   204	Core uses file-backed SQLite through Node 24 `node:sqlite`. A repository
   205	interface isolates synchronous database access from application and domain
   206	logic.
   207	
   208	Logical records cover:
   209	
   210	- scan identity and requested Git reference;
   211	- resolved immutable commit SHA;
   212	- target API version, kind, namespace, and name;
   213	- execution status, current stage, and timestamps;
   214	- supported desired and live field projections;
   215	- field-level differences and comparison outcome;
   216	- structured execution error;
   217	- explanation state, structured content, error, model identifier, and
   218	  timestamps; and
   219	- ordered stage transitions needed by the Core progress display.
   220	
   221	The database never stores:
   222	
   223	- Git or OpenAI tokens;
   224	- kubeconfig content;
   225	- complete desired or live manifests; or
   226	- unrelated Kubernetes fields.
   227	
   228	Core uses one scan record, one append-only scan-stage collection, and one
   229	explanation representation. Active-scan admission is atomic in SQLite rather
   230	than protected only by an in-memory flag.
   231	
   232	One idempotent schema bootstrap based on `PRAGMA user_version` and bounded
   233	`CREATE` statements runs during application startup. One connection serves
   234	the single process, and statements remain small and bounded. The database file
   235	lives on a persistent host path or container volume. SQLite fits one process
   236	and assessment-lifetime retention; an ORM, a general migration framework,
   237	PostgreSQL, and distributed coordination are deferred.
   238	
   239	`node:sqlite` is currently release-candidate stability. This accepted MVP
   240	trade-off removes an ORM and external native addon but makes Node 24 a runtime
   241	requirement. Local, CI, and deployment environments pin the same Node 24 patch
   242	or container image, and database-using routes explicitly use the Node.js
   243	runtime. A later stability problem can be contained behind the repository
   244	interface.
   245	
   246	## 7. AI explanation boundary
   247	
   248	The OpenAI adapter uses the official TypeScript SDK, Responses API, and
   249	Structured Outputs.
   250	
   251	Server-side configuration supplies:
   252	
   253	- `OPENAI_API_KEY`; and
   254	- `OPENAI_MODEL`, initially documented as `gpt-5.6`.
   255	
   256	The request contains only:
   257	
   258	- deterministic outcome;
   259	- supported desired and live field values;
   260	- field-level differences; and
   261	- bounded instructions for operator-focused analysis.
   262	
   263	It excludes credentials, repository authorization details, kubeconfig,
   264	complete manifests, unrelated fields, chat history, and remediation tools.
   265	
   266	The structured response contains:
   267	
   268	- summary;
   269	- important differences;
   270	- likely operational implications;
   271	- suggested investigation checks; and
   272	- limitations and uncertainty.
   273	
   274	The adapter validates the response before persistence. It does not retry
   275	automatically. Refusal, timeout, transport failure, invalid output, or provider
   276	failure becomes an explanation error and never alters scan truth.
   277	
   278	## 8. Runtime topology
   279	
   280	### Local
   281	
   282	- DriftLens runs as a long-lived Node.js process or Docker container on the
   283	  operator-controlled machine.
   284	- `kind` runs the private demo Kubernetes cluster.
   285	- The application reads a configured kubeconfig path.
   286	- SQLite uses a local persistent file.
   287	- The UI and API bind locally and are not publicly exposed.
   288	
   289	### Hosted demo
   290	
   291	- DriftLens remains outside Kubernetes, initially on [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] unless placement is
   292	  changed through an approved decision.
   293	- The private demo cluster runs separately from the DriftLens process.
   294	- CI and application identities remain isolated even if they share [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY].
   295	- The application uses an immutable build tied to the merged commit SHA.
   296	- Cloudflare-protected public access is an Extended step after local Core
   297	  acceptance; direct origin access must not bypass it.
   298	
   299	The exact container registry, process supervisor, domain, and Cloudflare
   300	configuration belong to the delivery specification.
   301	
   302	## 9. Security and trust boundaries
   303	
   304	### Product runtime
   305	
   306	- Validate every API, configuration, manifest, and external response boundary.
   307	- Keep secrets in runtime configuration only.
   308	- Mask sensitive values in structured logs and errors.
   309	- Mount kubeconfig and deployment credentials read-only where possible.
   310	- Use least-privilege Kubernetes RBAC.
   311	- Restrict GitHub source identity and transport.
   312	- Never mutate Kubernetes.
   313	- Never expose the local origin publicly without the approved external access
   314	  boundary.
   315	
   316	Core has no application-managed authentication or authorization. Local mode
   317	relies on operator-controlled network placement; hosted access relies on
   318	Cloudflare protection in Extended scope.
   319	
   320	### GitHub Actions
   321	
   322	This public repository uses self-hosted environments under a strict trust
   323	model:
   324	
   325	| Event | Self-hosted CI | Deployment access |
   326	| --- | --- | --- |
   327	| Push to canonical trusted issue branch | Allowed | None |
   328	| User-approved merge push to protected `main` | Full gates | Least-privilege demo deployment |
   329	| Fork or external pull-request event | Forbidden | Forbidden |
   330	| Comment or `pull_request_target` event | Forbidden | Forbidden |
   331	
   332	Workflows use canonical-repository `push` events only. External changes must be
   333	reviewed and copied into a trusted canonical branch before any execution.
   334	Workflow tokens are read-only by default, third-party Actions are pinned to
   335	immutable SHAs, and runner labels are not treated as a security boundary.
   336	
   337	CI and deployment need separate runner instances or isolated execution
   338	identities. CI must not have a deployment kubeconfig, Cloudflare credential,
   339	or broad home-lab access. The deployment identity accepts protected `main`
   340	pushes only.
   341	
   342	One workflow provides the delivery DAG:
   343	
   344	1. every trusted canonical branch push runs the verify job;
   345	2. the same `main` run continues to build one immutable SHA-tagged artifact;
   346	3. deployment waits for verify and build, then uses the isolated deployment
   347	   identity; and
   348	4. smoke verification proves the exact deployed revision.
   349	
   350	A single deployment concurrency group queues main revisions rather than
   351	cancelling an in-progress deployment. A second workflow must not duplicate the
   352	full verification or build.
   353	
   354	## 10. Observability and failure handling
   355	
   356	- Structured logs use levels and include scan and request correlation IDs.
   357	- Logs record stage transitions and error classes, never secret values or full
   358	  manifests.
   359	- Health reports process availability.
   360	- Readiness verifies required configuration and writable persistence without
   361	  depending on GitHub, Kubernetes, or OpenAI being continuously available.
   362	- API errors contain a stable machine-readable code and actionable safe
   363	  message.
   364	- Adapter failures are classified separately from comparison outcomes.
   365	
   366	Core stores enough state for the operator to understand a failed scan. It does
   367	not promise recovery of active work after process restart.

   373	- pure manifest projection and comparison behavior;

   375	- validation and safe error mapping;
   376	- explanation sanitization and structured response validation; and

   378	
   379	Unit tests perform no network access.
   380

   385	- SQLite migrations and history queries; and

   387

   390	- One parameterized React component test covers progress, result, history,

   394	- One named, single-node `kind` cluster is created by an idempotent demo script

   396	- The same demo cluster proves `IN_SYNC`, replica and image `DRIFTED`,

   399	- Explanation-provider failure remains deterministic test evidence rather than
   400	  another live-demo dependency.
   401	
   402	Release gates include formatting, lint, strict type checking, unit tests,
   403	production build, affected integration and end-to-end tests, dependency audit,

   417	| Structured AI output | Stable UI/persistence contract | Provider and model dependency |
   418	| DriftLens outside Kubernetes | Simple local and hosted operation | No in-cluster identity in Core |
   419	| Self-hosted push-only CI | Uses existing home-lab delivery path | External PRs receive no automatic CI |
   420	
   421	Deferred work remains defined by PRD MVP Extended and Future scope. In
   422	particular: configuration CRUD, private repositories, resource quantities,

   424	Cloudflare hosting, multiple clusters, scheduling, alerts, remediation,

## Scope

### Application scaffold

- Next.js App Router with TypeScript strict mode and npm lockfile.
- Node 24 pinned consistently for local, CI, and deployment.
- Minimal focused-console shell; no product workflow UI yet.
- Health, readiness, and immutable build-version API responses.
- Environment validation with safe actionable errors.
- ESLint, strict type check, Vitest, coverage command, production build, and dependency audit scripts.
- Multi-stage Docker image and minimal private-host runtime configuration.

### Trusted GitHub Actions path

- One workflow family triggered only by `push` in `RGCsAGupta/driftlens`.
- Trusted issue branches run verify: install, lint, type, unit, build, audit, and secret scan.
- `main` continues in the same run to immutable image/build, private [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] deployment, and exact-version health smoke.
- Deployment uses one non-cancelling concurrency group.
- Workflow token permissions are read-only by default.
- Every third-party Action is pinned to a full commit SHA.
- No `pull_request`, `pull_request_target`, issue-comment, fork, external-contributor, or automatic dependency-bot execution on self-hosted runners.

### Existing environment audit and reuse

Begin with a read-only inventory of the existing [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] self-hosted execution environment, isolated CI/deployment identities, and deployment permissions. Reuse working configuration; do not recreate or replace it.

The live DriftLens repository currently has no registered repository runner and no private demo deployment environment, so verify whether only repository binding is missing. If reuse requires a new runner host, execution identity, credential, permission expansion, or replacement of working configuration, stop and request a separate user decision.

### Repository controls

Approval of this specification authorizes only verified missing DriftLens repository bindings and controls:

- bind the existing isolated [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] CI and deployment execution environments to DriftLens as required;
- verify CI cannot access deployment kubeconfig, Cloudflare credentials, or broad home-lab resources;
- bind existing deployment permissions through a DriftLens environment restricted to `main`, without creating broader authority;

Registration tokens and credentials must never enter logs, prompts, issues, PRs, commits, or AI exports.

{"body":"## Goal

Deliver the first complete product workflow: start one real read-only scan from configured GitHub desired state to a live Kubernetes Deployment, persist progress/history, and retrieve exact deterministic results through the API.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Depends on: #8
Target budget: 52 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator value

A platform engineer can determine through independently accessible APIs whether the configured Deployment is in sync, drifted in replicas/images, or missing, while retaining actionable state and failures.

## Scope

### Server configuration

- One configured public GitHub `owner/repository` and safe relative YAML manifest path.
- One server-configured kubeconfig path and optional explicit context.
- Configuration is validated at startup and exposed only as non-secret source metadata.
- API accepts a branch or commit SHA per scan and records the resolved immutable SHA.

### API capabilities

- Start a scan and return `202` with scan identity and queued status.
- Retrieve one scan with status, stage transitions, target, resolved SHA, outcome, differences, and safe error.
- List bounded newest-first history with a default limit and enforced maximum.
- Return a structured conflict while another scan is active.
- Return non-secret configured source metadata needed by the UI.

Exact paths and Zod schemas are defined in the implementation and documented in the PR/README.

### Workflow

Persist and expose:

1. queued;
2. loading desired manifest;
3. reading live Deployment;
4. comparing supported fields;
5. saving result; and
6. completed or failed.

Use self-hosted Next.js `after()` for the in-process task. Admission is atomic in SQLite. There is no automatic retry, cancellation, overall workflow timeout, concurrency, or restart resumability. Every external transport call has a bounded timeout.

### Desired state

- Resolve branch/SHA through GitHub REST.
- Fetch exactly one file at the resolved SHA.
- Plain YAML, one document, one `apps/v1` Deployment.
- Require explicit name and namespace.
- Reject unsafe path, wrong kind/version, multiple documents, or malformed manifest.

### Live state and comparison

- Read exactly the matching namespaced Deployment with `@kubernetes/client-node`.
- Use read-only Kubernetes access; perform no list/watch/write operation.
- Compare `spec.replicas`, defaulting omitted desired replicas to `1`.
- Match desired regular containers by name and compare exact image strings.
- Desired container missing live reports drift.
- Extra live-only containers are ignored.
- Init/ephemeral containers and unrelated/runtime-owned fields are ignored.
- Produce only `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, or `MISSING_LIVE` as comparison outcomes.
- Git, manifest, authorization, availability, timeout, and internal failures produce typed execution errors, never drift.

### Persistence

Use Node 24 `node:sqlite` with one idempotent schema-version-1 `PRAGMA user_version` bootstrap, one connection, atomic active-scan admission, a scan record, and append-only stage records. All dynamic values use prepared, parameterized statements; only fixed schema bootstrap statements may execute as static SQL.

Persist only PRD-approved projections, differences, timestamps, resolved SHA, outcome, and safe errors. Never persist complete manifests, kubeconfig, credentials, or unrelated fields.

A bootstrap or admission write failure returns a safe synchronous service error and creates no scan. After successful admission, terminal failure persistence is best effort: if SQLite itself cannot write the terminal record, readiness, correlated structured logs, and the API expose a safe storage failure without claiming that failed history was durably recorded. Core does not resume the stale workflow automatically.

## Non-goals

- Operator workflow UI beyond API inspection.
- AI explanation.
- CPU or memory quantities.
- Configuration CRUD or private Git.
- Detailed event log, cancellation, retry, timeout status, or restart recovery.
- Discovery, scheduling, remediation, or additional Kubernetes resources.
- Live kind proof; the release issue supplies the single bounded live demo.

## Acceptance criteria

- Starting a valid scan returns immediately and stage/status polling observes persisted progress.
- Branch input resolves and stores its immutable commit SHA.
- `IN_SYNC` is exact for matching replicas and every desired container image.
- Replica drift, image drift, and missing desired containers produce field-level differences.
- Extra live-only containers do not produce drift.
- Kubernetes 404 becomes `MISSING_LIVE` and a completed scan.
- Invalid manifest, unsupported resource, Git failure, Kubernetes denial/unavailability, and transport timeout are actionable persisted execution failures when storage remains available.
- Bootstrap/admission storage failure returns synchronously without a scan; post-admission storage failure is exposed safely without a false durable-history claim.
- History survives application restart and returns bounded newest-first results.
- A concurrent start attempt returns conflict without creating a second active workflow.
- API responses and logs contain no credentials or complete manifests.

## Test evidence

- Unit happy: replicas/images in sync.
- Unit edges: omitted replicas, name-based reordered containers, extra live sidecar ignored, missing desired container, multiple differences.
- Unit failures: malformed/multi-document/wrong-resource manifest and safe error mapping.
- Workflow happy: fake GitHub/Kubernetes adapters drive every stage to persisted completion.
- Workflow failures: each adapter/stage failure persists the correct terminal error; no automatic retry calls occur.
- Persistence: version-1 bootstrap idempotency, prepared-statement binding, injection-safe dynamic values, atomic admission, ordered stages, restart history, and bounded query.
- Storage failures: bootstrap/admission failure creates no scan; post-admission write failure proves best-effort terminal handling plus safe readiness, log, and API evidence.
- API: validation, `202`, polling detail, history, not-found, and active conflict.
- Security: fake Kubernetes client asserts read-only Deployment operation and sanitized persistence/logging.

## Documentation

Document non-secret configuration, API capability examples, comparison semantics, error taxonomy, persistence boundary, and Core limitations.

## Rollback

Revert the application commit and redeploy the last known-good artifact. Database bootstrap must be backward-safe for this issue; if a schema rollback is unsafe, preserve the file and document recovery rather than deleting history.

{"body":"## Goal

Allow the operator to manually request and persist a short structured explanation for every completed comparison outcome without letting AI determine or alter drift.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Depends on: #8, #9, and #10
Target budget: 14 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator value

An operator receives concise analysis of deterministic differences, implications, investigation checks, and uncertainty while retaining the exact field-level result as source of truth.

## Scope

### Explanation API and state

- Add a manual explanation request capability for completed `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE` scans.
- Persist explanation state independently from scan execution: not requested, requested, saved, or failed.
- Return an existing saved explanation idempotently without another provider call.
- Reject non-completed/failed scan requests with a structured conflict.
- A failed Core explanation is terminal; there is no automatic or manual explanation retry.
- Scan status and deterministic outcome remain unchanged for every explanation state.

### OpenAI adapter

- Use the official TypeScript SDK, Responses API, and Structured Outputs.
- Read `OPENAI_API_KEY` and configurable `OPENAI_MODEL` server-side; document `gpt-5.6` as the initial value.
- Apply one bounded transport timeout and zero automatic retries.
- Validate structured fields: summary, important differences, likely implications, investigation checks, and limitations/uncertainty.
- Detect refusal, incomplete/invalid output, timeout, and provider errors and persist a safe explanation error.

### Sanitization

Provider input contains only:

- comparison outcome;
- supported desired/live replicas and image values;
- container/field identities and deterministic differences; and
- bounded operator-analysis instructions.

It excludes tokens, kubeconfig, repository authorization details, complete manifests, unrelated Kubernetes fields, raw logs/errors, history, and remediation tools.

### UI integration

- Show “Explain result” only for completed comparison outcomes.
- Require an explicit operator click.
- Show requested/loading, structured explanation, saved explanation, and failed states.
- Clearly label the content as AI-generated analysis and preserve the deterministic result above it.
- Do not add chat, charts, streaming text, or remediation controls.

## Non-goals

- AI drift classification, root-cause confirmation, remediation, or tool calls.
- Interactive chat or follow-up questions.
- Automatic explanation generation or retry.
- Full manifests, cluster inspection, or external retrieval by the model.
- Provider fallback or multi-model routing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Operator can manually request an explanation for each completed comparison outcome.
- Exactly one sanitized provider request occurs for a new explanation.
- Saved explanation survives restart and is returned without another call.
- Scan execution status/outcome never changes when explanation succeeds or fails.
- Provider payload contains only the allowlisted deterministic projection.
- Structured explanation renders all required operator-analysis sections.
- Refusal, invalid output, timeout, absent configuration, and provider failure produce safe persisted explanation errors.
- No automatic retry occurs.
- API/UI/logs never expose the OpenAI key or excluded scan data.

## Test evidence

- Happy: structured explanation saved and rendered for `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE`.
- Edge: already-saved explanation is idempotent; concurrent duplicate request does not duplicate provider calls.
- Failures: refusal, malformed structured output, timeout, missing key/model, and provider error.
- Security: payload allowlist assertion and secret/log scan.
- Truth boundary: explicit assertions that scan status, outcome, and differences are byte-for-byte unchanged after every explanation path.
- Unit tests use a fake OpenAI adapter and no network.

## Documentation

Document server-side AI configuration, sanitized payload boundary, structured output, limitations, cost/provider dependency, no-retry behavior, and proof that AI is not drift truth.

## Rollback

Disable the explanation capability and revert the application commit while preserving existing deterministic scans. A persistence change must be additive or backward-safe; never delete scan history during rollback.

{"body":"## Goal

Finish MVP Core with one reproducible real-cluster demonstration, exact-revision deployment proof, complete assessment documentation, and secret-safe submission evidence.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Depends on: #8, #9, #10, and #11

## Operator and reviewer value

A reviewer can clone the public repository, run the application locally, observe a real Git-to-Kubernetes workflow through UI and API, inspect design trade-offs and Git history, and verify every assessment deliverable.

## Scope

### Demo desired state and cluster

- Keep one simple public `apps/v1` Deployment manifest in the repository for the configured desired source.
- Provide an idempotent script to create one named, single-node `kind` cluster with a pinned node image and bounded readiness wait.
- Create a dedicated namespace and least-privilege read-only credential/kubeconfig for DriftLens.
- RBAC permits only the Deployment read capability required by the configured target; no mutation through DriftLens credentials.
- DriftLens runs outside the cluster.

### One bounded demo sequence

Using the same cluster and configured manifest:

1. `IN_SYNC`: desired and live replicas/images match.
2. `DRIFTED`: controlled live replica and image changes produce exact differences.
3. `MISSING_LIVE`: delete the live Deployment and scan the desired manifest.
4. Failure and recovery: use an invalid configured source/path or bounded cluster-access failure, verify actionable failure in history, restore configuration/access, then start a normal successful scan. This is not retry.
5. Manually request and display one structured AI explanation for a completed drift outcome.

The demo setup may mutate its disposable cluster through explicit demo scripts; the DriftLens application and credential remain read-only.

### Local setup and final verification

- Clean-clone instructions cover prerequisites, configuration, kind setup, app startup, demo sequence, teardown, and common failures.
- One command or short documented command sequence runs lint, type, unit, build, integration, and the bounded operator flow.
- One real kind proof supplies live integration; do not duplicate cluster creation across normal unit/CI suites.
- Explanation-provider failure remains deterministic fake evidence rather than a required live-provider failure.

### Main deployment proof

- User-approved merge to protected `main` triggers the single verify → immutable build → private deploy → exact-revision smoke DAG.
- Prove the deployed version/health corresponds to the merge commit or artifact digest.
- Do not expose the origin publicly in Core.
- Cloudflare, domain selection, private Git configuration, and public hosted access remain Extended work.

### Submission package

- Comprehensive README: setup, use-case rationale, workflow, demo, API usage, testing, design decisions, security boundaries, trade-offs, limitations, and troubleshooting.
- Architecture overview finalized from PR #7.
- “What next” writeup maps MVP Extended/Future work and production hardening.
- Assessment matrix in PRD/release issue links exact evidence.
- Meaningful Git history review.
- Exact command, CI run URL, deployment SHA/digest, read-only RBAC, and demo evidence.
- Complete AI interaction inventory and full secret-reviewed exports for every user-facing session and delegated-agent prompt, relevant interaction, result, owner review, correction, and final outcome. Summaries do not replace full available transcripts. Use an explicit redaction manifest when needed, and carry forward any evidence blocker found by the #8 preflight.
- Useful screenshots or short recording for UI stages/outcomes if time remains.
- Final known-risk and failed-gate record.

## Non-goals

- Cloudflare or public-domain exposure.
- Private repository configuration or CRUD.
- CPU/memory resource drift.
- Cancellation, retry, timeout status, discovery, in-cluster DriftLens, or Extended scope.
- Production HA, backups, audit retention, or multi-user authentication.

## Acceptance criteria

- A clean clone completes the documented local setup.
- DriftLens UI and API execute a real read-only GitHub-to-kind scan.
- All four comparison/demo scenarios and actionable failure/recovery are retained in history.
- Replica and image differences are exact; extra live sidecars remain ignored if demonstrated/tested.
- Manual AI explanation works for a completed outcome; deterministic truth remains unchanged.
- Dedicated kubeconfig fails attempted Deployment mutation while required read succeeds.
- Full local quality pyramid passes on the final exact head.
- Protected-main merge automatically deploys and smoke-verifies the exact revision privately.
- README, architecture, trade-offs, next-work, API, demo, and security documentation are complete.
- Every assessment requirement in #3 links retained evidence.
- Complete secret-safe user-facing and delegated-agent interaction exports are present, including prompts, available interaction/tool records, results, owner reviews, corrections, and final outcomes; summaries are not substituted for required full logs.
- The session inventory reconciles every delegation to an export location or an explicitly recorded submission blocker.
- Final repository secret scan and dependency audit pass.

## Test and evidence requirements

- Unit: happy, edge, and failure coverage for every changed module.
- Integration: SQLite/API contracts plus the one authorized real kind proof.
- End-to-end: one-worker, zero-retry Chromium critical operator flow.
- Security: read-only RBAC denial proof, workflow trust audit, credential/log/export scan.
- Delivery: GitHub Actions URLs, exact source SHA, artifact identity, deployment health/version, and rollback note.
- Documentation: commands executed from a clean clone or equivalent isolated checkout.

ISSUE #8 [Foundation] Establish the runnable app and trusted delivery path
## Goal

Create the smallest runnable DriftLens foundation and prove that only trusted canonical-repository pushes can use the self-hosted CI/deployment path.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Target budget: 18 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator value

A clean clone runs a recognizable DriftLens shell with health, readiness, and version evidence. Every later issue inherits a working test/build/container/deployment path rather than deferring integration risk.

## Scope

### Application scaffold

- Next.js App Router with TypeScript strict mode and npm lockfile.
- Node 24 pinned consistently for local, CI, and deployment.
- Minimal focused-console shell; no product workflow UI yet.
- Health, readiness, and immutable build-version API responses.
- Environment validation with safe actionable errors.
- ESLint, strict type check, Vitest, coverage command, production build, and dependency audit scripts.
- Multi-stage Docker image and minimal configuration for the reused Proxmox/Cloudflare-protected runtime.
- Baseline README instructions for install, checks, build, and local start.

### Trusted GitHub Actions path

- One workflow family triggered only by `push` in `RGCsAGupta/driftlens`.
- Trusted issue branches run verify: install, lint, type, unit, build, audit, and secret scan.
- `main` continues in the same run to immutable image/build, deployment through the existing Proxmox/Cloudflare-protected path, and exact-version health smoke.
- Deployment uses one non-cancelling concurrency group.
- Workflow token permissions are read-only by default.
- Every third-party Action is pinned to a full commit SHA.
- No `pull_request`, `pull_request_target`, issue-comment, fork, external-contributor, or automatic dependency-bot execution on self-hosted runners.

### Existing environment audit and reuse

Begin with a read-only inventory of the existing [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] self-hosted execution environment, isolated CI/deployment identities, deployment permissions, and Cloudflare-protected route. Reuse working configuration; do not recreate or replace it.

The live DriftLens repository currently has no registered repository runner and no private demo deployment environment, so verify whether only repository binding is missing. If reuse requires a new runner host, execution identity, credential, permission expansion, or replacement of working configuration, stop and request a separate user decision.

### Repository controls

Approval of this specification authorizes only verified missing DriftLens repository bindings and controls:

- bind the existing isolated [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] CI and deployment execution environments to DriftLens as required;
- verify CI cannot access deployment kubeconfig, Cloudflare credentials, or broad home-lab resources;
- verify and reuse the existing Cloudflare route and access policy without creating or expanding either;
- bind existing deployment permissions through a DriftLens environment restricted to `main`, without creating broader authority;
- protect `main` against direct push, force-push, and deletion;
- require pull requests and the verified branch check before merge; and
- retain the user as the only write principal unless the user explicitly adds a collaborator.

Registration tokens and credentials must never enter logs, prompts, issues, PRs, commits, or AI exports.

### AI interaction evidence preflight

Before delegating implementation, verify that the export process preserves each delegated-agent prompt, relevant interaction, result, owner review, correction, and final outcome. Start the session inventory and secret-review procedure. If the platform export omits delegated interactions and no complete separate export is available, do not delegate implementation and record the evidence blocker.

## Non-goals

- Scan workflow, GitHub manifest loading, Kubernetes access, SQLite history, or OpenAI.
- New public DNS, a new or expanded Cloudflare route/access policy, or a new Proxmox environment.
- Kubernetes deployment of DriftLens.
- Product UI beyond a recognizable shell.
- External-contributor CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- Clean clone succeeds with documented Node 24 and npm commands.
- Local UI, health, readiness, and build-version endpoints run.
- Lint, type, unit, coverage, production build, dependency audit, and secret scan pass.
- Docker image builds and reports the injected exact commit SHA.
- DriftLens is bound to the verified existing isolated self-hosted execution environments without recreating working host-side configuration.
- A canonical issue-branch push runs verify without deployment access.
- Fork/PR/comment triggers cannot schedule a self-hosted job by workflow inspection and repository settings.
- `main` protection blocks direct pushes and requires the verified check.
- A user-approved merge push runs verify, build, deployment through the reused protected path, and exact-revision smoke without a second approval.
- The protected endpoint reports the exact merged revision, and direct origin bypass is unavailable.
- No secret or sensitive home-lab value appears in retained evidence.
- AI export preflight proves delegated interactions can be completely captured and secret-reviewed before any implementation delegation.

## Test evidence

- Happy: local and container health/version checks pass.
- Edge: missing non-secret required configuration produces a safe readiness failure.
- Failure: a deliberately failing unit check blocks build/deploy in a controlled test or workflow-level fixture; do not merge broken code.
- Security: workflow-event audit proves no externally triggerable self-hosted event and deployment credentials are unavailable to verify jobs.

## Documentation

Update README foundation setup, required non-secret variables, check commands, the reused protected deployment path, and its limitations. Record exact runner labels only if they reveal no sensitive infrastructure detail.

## Dependencies

- User-approved architecture issue #4.
- PR #7 merged before this implementation PR is ready.
- [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] access and existing host-side and Cloudflare-protected deployment prerequisites.

## Rollback

Redeploy the last known-good immutable artifact. Revert repository setting changes only with explicit user approval. Remove a runner registration only after confirming no active job and preserving evidence.


ISSUE #9 [Core] Scan one Deployment and persist deterministic history
## Goal

Deliver the first complete product workflow: start one real read-only scan from configured GitHub desired state to a live Kubernetes Deployment, persist progress/history, and retrieve exact deterministic results through the API.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Depends on: #8
Target budget: 52 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator value

A platform engineer can determine through independently accessible APIs whether the configured Deployment is in sync, drifted in replicas/images, or missing, while retaining actionable state and failures.

## Scope

### Server configuration

- One configured public GitHub `owner/repository` and safe relative YAML manifest path.
- One server-configured kubeconfig path and optional explicit context.
- Configuration is validated at startup and exposed only as non-secret source metadata.
- API accepts a branch or commit SHA per scan and records the resolved immutable SHA.

### API capabilities

- Start a scan and return `202` with scan identity and queued status.
- Retrieve one scan with status, stage transitions, target, resolved SHA, outcome, differences, and safe error.
- List bounded newest-first history with a default limit and enforced maximum.
- Return a structured conflict while another scan is active.
- Return non-secret configured source metadata needed by the UI.

Exact paths and Zod schemas are defined in the implementation and documented in the PR/README.

### Workflow

Persist and expose:

1. queued;
2. loading desired manifest;
3. reading live Deployment;
4. comparing supported fields;
5. saving result; and
6. completed or failed.

Use self-hosted Next.js `after()` for the in-process task. A simple in-memory coordinator admits at most one active scan in the current process and returns conflict for a second request. There is no automatic retry, cancellation, overall workflow timeout, concurrent-scan support, advanced locking, or restart resumability. Every external transport call has a bounded timeout.

### Desired state

- Resolve branch/SHA through GitHub REST.
- Fetch exactly one file at the resolved SHA.
- Plain YAML, one document, one `apps/v1` Deployment.
- Require explicit name and namespace.
- Reject unsafe path, wrong kind/version, multiple documents, or malformed manifest.

### Live state and comparison

- Read exactly the matching namespaced Deployment with `@kubernetes/client-node`.
- Use read-only Kubernetes access; perform no list/watch/write operation.
- Compare `spec.replicas`, defaulting omitted desired replicas to `1`.
- Match desired regular containers by name and compare exact image strings.
- Desired container missing live reports drift.
- Extra live-only containers are ignored.
- Init/ephemeral containers and unrelated/runtime-owned fields are ignored.
- Produce only `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, or `MISSING_LIVE` as comparison outcomes.
- Git, manifest, authorization, availability, timeout, and internal failures produce typed execution errors, never drift.

### Persistence

Use Node 24 `node:sqlite` with one idempotent schema-version-1 `PRAGMA user_version` bootstrap, one connection, a scan record, and append-only stage records. All dynamic values use prepared, parameterized statements; only fixed schema bootstrap statements may execute as static SQL.

Persist only PRD-approved projections, differences, timestamps, resolved SHA, outcome, and safe errors. Never persist complete manifests, kubeconfig, credentials, or unrelated fields.

A bootstrap or initial scan write failure releases the in-memory coordinator, returns a safe synchronous service error, and creates no scan. After the queued scan is persisted, terminal failure persistence is best effort: if SQLite itself cannot write the terminal record, readiness, correlated structured logs, and the API expose a safe storage failure without claiming that failed history was durably recorded. Core does not resume the stale workflow automatically.

The coordinator exists only in the current process. Restart clears that marker; any prior `QUEUED` or `RUNNING` record remains unchanged as evidence. Core does not resume, complete, delete, or otherwise recover it, and the new process may start a new scan.

## Non-goals

- Operator workflow UI beyond API inspection.
- AI explanation.
- CPU or memory quantities.
- Configuration CRUD or private Git.
- Detailed event log, cancellation, retry, timeout status, or restart recovery.
- Discovery, scheduling, remediation, or additional Kubernetes resources.
- Live kind proof; the release issue supplies the single bounded live demo.

## Acceptance criteria

- Starting a valid scan returns immediately and stage/status polling observes persisted progress.
- Branch input resolves and stores its immutable commit SHA.
- `IN_SYNC` is exact for matching replicas and every desired container image.
- Replica drift, image drift, and missing desired containers produce field-level differences.
- Extra live-only containers do not produce drift.
- Kubernetes 404 becomes `MISSING_LIVE` and a completed scan.
- Invalid manifest, unsupported resource, Git failure, Kubernetes denial/unavailability, and transport timeout are actionable persisted execution failures when storage remains available.
- Bootstrap/initial-scan storage failure returns synchronously without a scan; later storage failure is exposed safely without a false durable-history claim.
- History survives application restart and returns bounded newest-first results.
- A concurrent start attempt returns conflict without creating a second active workflow.
- After restart, the new in-memory coordinator admits a new scan and leaves any stale prior record unchanged.
- API responses and logs contain no credentials or complete manifests.

## Test evidence

- Unit happy: replicas/images in sync.
- Unit edges: omitted replicas, name-based reordered containers, extra live sidecar ignored, missing desired container, multiple differences.
- Unit failures: malformed/multi-document/wrong-resource manifest and safe error mapping.
- Workflow happy: fake GitHub/Kubernetes adapters drive every stage to persisted completion.
- Workflow failures: each adapter/stage failure persists the correct terminal error; no automatic retry calls occur.
- Persistence: version-1 bootstrap idempotency, prepared-statement binding, injection-safe dynamic values, ordered stages, restart history, and bounded query.
- Storage failures: bootstrap/initial-scan failure creates no scan; later write failure proves best-effort terminal handling plus safe readiness, log, and API evidence.
- Restart coordinator: a new process can start a scan while the stale prior record remains neither resumed, completed, deleted, nor modified.
- API: validation, `202`, polling detail, history, not-found, and active conflict.
- Security: fake Kubernetes client asserts read-only Deployment operation and sanitized persistence/logging.

## Documentation

Document non-secret configuration, API capability examples, comparison semantics, error taxonomy, persistence boundary, and Core limitations.

## Rollback

Revert the application commit and redeploy the last known-good artifact. Database bootstrap must be backward-safe for this issue; if a schema rollback is unsafe, preserve the file and document recovery rather than deleting history.



ISSUE #10 [Core] Deliver the focused operator scan console
## Goal

Deliver the focused operator console that consumes the scan APIs and makes initiation, progress, deterministic results, history, and failures transparent.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Depends on: #8 and #9
Target budget: 27 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator value

A platform engineer or SRE can complete and understand the real DriftLens workflow without inspecting raw API payloads or logs.

## Scope

### Console shell

- Show DriftLens purpose and configured public repository/manifest path without exposing credentials.
- Provide one branch-or-SHA input and primary “Run scan” action.
- Disable or replace the action with an explicit busy state while a scan is active.
- Remain a focused console, not a monitoring dashboard.

### Progress and outcome

- Poll the backend while the scan is queued/running.
- Show current [REDACTED: CREDENTIAL] and terminal execution status.
- Present `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE` distinctly without using color alone.
- For drift, show a compact field-level table with field/container identity, desired value, and live value.
- Show resolved commit SHA and Deployment namespace/name.
- Render actionable safe failure text with a stable error category.

### History

- Show bounded newest-first history with time, target, execution status, and comparison outcome.
- Open a previous scan without starting another workflow.
- Refresh history after terminal completion.
- Preserve selected scan identity in the URL where practical; do not use browser local storage.

### Interaction and accessibility

- Keyboard-operable controls, visible focus, labeled form input, semantic status text, and accessible loading indication.
- Responsive layout for normal laptop widths.
- Prevent duplicate submissions and stale polling updates.
- Stop polling at a terminal state and show safe retry-by-new-scan guidance for failures; no retry feature is implemented.

## Non-goals

- Repository or target configuration UI.
- AI explanation controls; issue #11 adds them.
- Charts, trends, monitoring dashboard, bulk actions, or live streaming.
- Cancellation, retry, timeout, discovery, authentication, or multi-user behavior.
- Full manifest display or raw error/log viewer.

## Acceptance criteria

- Operator can start a real scan through the API from the UI.
- Every Core stage is visibly understandable while polling.
- In-sync, replica drift, image drift, missing live, and failed execution render correctly.
- Drift table displays exact supported desired/live values and container names.
- History and previous details remain usable after page reload without local storage.
- Active scan prevents duplicate submission.
- Polling stops on completion/failure and does not overwrite a newly selected history item.
- UI never displays secrets, kubeconfig, tokens, complete manifests, or unsafe backend details.
- Layout and controls pass the agreed [REDACTED: CREDENTIAL] checks.

## Test evidence

- Component happy: queued → stages → completed in-sync.
- Component edges: multiple replica/image differences, missing live, empty history, and long safe messages.
- Component failure: backend validation/execution error and polling transport failure remain actionable.
- Parameterized rendering test covers status/outcome/history variants without duplicated suites.
- One-worker, zero-retry Chromium Playwright flow covers start, progress, result, and history using controlled adapters.
- Accessibility smoke covers labels, roles, focus, keyboard operation, and non-color status cues.
- Production build and existing backend suites remain green.

## Documentation

Add operator workflow screenshots only when stable and useful. Update README usage, visible statuses, and UI limitations.

## Rollback

Revert the UI commit and redeploy the last known-good artifact. No persistence migration is introduced by this issue.
ISSUE #11 [Core] Add manual sanitized AI explanations
## Goal

Allow the operator to manually request and persist a short structured explanation for every completed comparison outcome without letting AI determine or alter drift.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Depends on: #8, #9, and #10
Target budget: 14 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator value

An operator receives concise analysis of deterministic differences, implications, investigation checks, and uncertainty while retaining the exact field-level result as source of truth.

## Scope

### Explanation API and state

- Add a manual explanation request capability for completed `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE` scans.
- Persist explanation state independently from scan execution: not requested, requested, saved, or failed.
- Return an existing saved explanation idempotently without another provider call.
- Reject non-completed/failed scan requests with a structured conflict.
- A failed Core explanation is terminal; there is no automatic or manual explanation retry.
- Scan status and deterministic outcome remain unchanged for every explanation state.

### OpenAI adapter

- Use the official TypeScript SDK, Responses API, and Structured Outputs.
- Read `OPENAI_API_KEY` and configurable `OPENAI_MODEL` server-side; document `gpt-5.6` as the initial value.
- Apply one bounded transport timeout and zero automatic retries.
- Validate structured fields: summary, important differences, likely implications, investigation checks, and limitations/uncertainty.
- Detect refusal, incomplete/invalid output, timeout, and provider errors and persist a safe explanation error.

### Sanitization

Provider input contains only:

- comparison outcome;
- supported desired/live replicas and image values;
- container/field identities and deterministic differences; and
- bounded operator-analysis instructions.

It excludes tokens, kubeconfig, repository authorization details, complete manifests, unrelated Kubernetes fields, raw logs/errors, history, and remediation tools.

### UI integration

- Show “Explain result” only for completed comparison outcomes.
- Require an explicit operator click.
- Show requested/loading, structured explanation, saved explanation, and failed states.
- Clearly label the content as AI-generated analysis and preserve the deterministic result above it.
- Do not add chat, charts, streaming text, or remediation controls.

## Non-goals

- AI drift classification, root-cause confirmation, remediation, or tool calls.
- Interactive chat or follow-up questions.
- Automatic explanation generation or retry.
- Full manifests, cluster inspection, or external retrieval by the model.
- Provider fallback or multi-model routing.
- Concurrent explanation-request coordination; Core only guarantees idempotent reuse after an explanation has been saved.

## Acceptance criteria

- Operator can manually request an explanation for each completed comparison outcome.
- Exactly one sanitized provider request occurs for a new explanation.
- Saved explanation survives restart and is returned without another call.
- Scan execution status/outcome never changes when explanation succeeds or fails.
- Provider payload contains only the allowlisted deterministic projection.
- Structured explanation renders all required operator-analysis sections.
- Refusal, invalid output, timeout, absent configuration, and provider failure produce safe persisted explanation errors.
- No automatic retry occurs.
- API/UI/logs never expose the OpenAI key or excluded scan data.

## Test evidence

- Happy: structured explanation saved and rendered for `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE`.
- Edge: an already-saved explanation is returned idempotently without another provider call.
- Failures: refusal, malformed structured output, timeout, missing key/model, and provider error.
- Security: payload allowlist assertion and secret/log scan.
- Truth boundary: explicit assertions that scan status, outcome, and differences are byte-for-byte unchanged after every explanation path.
- Unit tests use a fake OpenAI adapter and no network.

## Documentation

Document server-side AI configuration, sanitized payload boundary, structured output, limitations, cost/provider dependency, no-retry behavior, and proof that AI is not drift truth.

## Rollback

Disable the explanation capability and revert the application commit while preserving existing deterministic scans. A persistence change must be additive or backward-safe; never delete scan history during rollback.


ISSUE #12 [Release] Prove the local demo, deployment, and submission evidence
## Goal

Finish MVP Core with one reproducible real-cluster demonstration, exact-revision deployment proof, complete assessment documentation, and secret-safe submission evidence.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Depends on: #8, #9, #10, and #11
Target budget: 42 active minutes plus only the remaining risk reserve, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator and reviewer value

A reviewer can clone the public repository, run the application locally, observe a real Git-to-Kubernetes workflow through UI and API, inspect design trade-offs and Git history, and verify every assessment deliverable.

## Scope

### Demo desired state and cluster

- Keep one simple public `apps/v1` Deployment manifest in the repository for the configured desired source.
- Provide an idempotent script to create one named, single-node `kind` cluster with a pinned node image and bounded readiness wait.
- Create a dedicated namespace and least-privilege read-only credential/kubeconfig for DriftLens.
- RBAC permits only the Deployment read capability required by the configured target; no mutation through DriftLens credentials.
- DriftLens runs outside the cluster.

### One bounded demo sequence

Using the same cluster and configured manifest:

1. `IN_SYNC`: desired and live replicas/images match.
2. `DRIFTED`: controlled live replica and image changes produce exact differences.
3. `MISSING_LIVE`: delete the live Deployment and scan the desired manifest.
4. Failure and recovery: use an invalid configured source/path or bounded cluster-access failure, verify actionable failure in history, restore configuration/access, then start a normal successful scan. This is not retry.
5. Manually request and display one structured AI explanation for a completed drift outcome.

The demo setup may mutate its disposable cluster through explicit demo scripts; the DriftLens application and credential remain read-only.

### Local setup and final verification

- Clean-clone instructions cover prerequisites, configuration, kind setup, app startup, demo sequence, teardown, and common failures.
- One command or short documented command sequence runs lint, type, unit, build, integration, and the bounded operator flow.
- One real kind proof supplies live integration; do not duplicate cluster creation across normal unit/CI suites.
- Explanation-provider failure remains deterministic fake evidence rather than a required live-provider failure.

### Main deployment proof

- User-approved merge to protected `main` triggers the single verify → immutable build → deployment through the existing Proxmox/Cloudflare-protected path → exact-revision smoke DAG.
- Prove through the protected endpoint that the deployed version/health corresponds to the merge commit or artifact digest.
- Verify direct origin bypass is unavailable.
- A new or expanded Cloudflare route, access policy, domain, deployment identity, or Proxmox environment remains a separate user decision; private Git configuration remains Extended work.

### Submission package

- Comprehensive README: setup, use-case rationale, workflow, demo, API usage, testing, design decisions, security boundaries, trade-offs, limitations, and troubleshooting.
- Architecture overview finalized from PR #7.
- “What next” writeup maps MVP Extended/Future work and production hardening.
- Assessment matrix in PRD/release issue links exact evidence.
- Meaningful Git history review.
- Exact command, CI run URL, deployment SHA/digest, read-only RBAC, and demo evidence.
- Complete AI interaction inventory and full secret-reviewed exports for every user-facing session and delegated-agent prompt, relevant interaction, result, owner review, correction, and final outcome. Summaries do not replace full available transcripts. Use an explicit redaction manifest when needed, and carry forward any evidence blocker found by the #8 preflight.
- Useful screenshots or short recording for UI stages/outcomes if time remains.
- Final known-risk and failed-gate record.

## Non-goals

- New or expanded Cloudflare/Proxmox infrastructure, route, access policy, domain, or deployment permission.
- Private repository configuration or CRUD.
- CPU/memory resource drift.
- Cancellation, retry, timeout status, discovery, in-cluster DriftLens, or Extended scope.
- Production HA, backups, audit retention, or multi-user authentication.

## Acceptance criteria

- A clean clone completes the documented local setup.
- DriftLens UI and API execute a real read-only GitHub-to-kind scan.
- All four comparison/demo scenarios and actionable failure/recovery are retained in history.
- Replica and image differences are exact; extra live sidecars remain ignored if demonstrated/tested.
- Manual AI explanation works for a completed outcome; deterministic truth remains unchanged.
- Dedicated kubeconfig fails attempted Deployment mutation while required read succeeds.
- Full local quality pyramid passes on the final exact head.
- Protected-main merge automatically deploys and smoke-verifies the exact revision through the reused Cloudflare-protected endpoint.
- README, architecture, trade-offs, next-work, API, demo, and security documentation are complete.
- Every assessment requirement in #3 links retained evidence.
- Complete secret-safe user-facing and delegated-agent interaction exports are present, including prompts, available interaction/tool records, results, owner reviews, corrections, and final outcomes; summaries are not substituted for required full logs.
- The session inventory reconciles every delegation to an export location or an explicitly recorded submission blocker.
- Final repository secret scan and dependency audit pass.

## Test and evidence requirements

- Unit: happy, edge, and failure coverage for every changed module.
- Integration: SQLite/API contracts plus the one authorized real kind proof.
- End-to-end: one-worker, zero-retry Chromium critical operator flow.
- Security: read-only RBAC denial proof, workflow trust audit, credential/log/export scan.
- Delivery: GitHub Actions URLs, exact source SHA, artifact identity, deployment health/version, and rollback note.
- Documentation: commands executed from a clean clone or equivalent isolated checkout.

## Documentation

This issue owns the final README, demo guide, next-work writeup, assessment evidence index, AI-export inventory, and known-limitations/risk record.

## Rollback and teardown

Redeploy the last known-good immutable artifact if smoke fails. Preserve the SQLite evidence file unless corruption requires user-directed recovery. Demo-cluster teardown is explicit and targets only the named disposable cluster. Runner, environment, Cloudflare, DNS, credential, or other control-plane mutation or deletion beyond the approved reuse requires explicit user approval.
